# Trueup Witness

**Your dashboard said OK. Your agent crashed. Trueup turns on the DISAGREE light.**

**[Crash it yourself, live →](https://trueup.38-49-216-59.sslip.io)** Break a real AI bot with one click.

Every fix links to the Entire record of the session that made it: see fixes/<id>/PROVENANCE.md.

Planes warn pilots when two readings disagree. AI teams trust one instrument: the tracing record. Witness watches what really happened and compares it with what neatlogs recorded.

```python
import trueup.witness
trueup.witness.watch()
```

When the record is wrong, Witness adds a red `TRACE DISAGREE` step to the same neatlogs trace. It never sends prompt or reply text beyond what neatlogs already records, never breaks your app, and turns off with `TRUEUP_WITNESS=0`.

## Live result

Real Claude Haiku and OpenAI Agents calls, before and after Trueup's patches:

| Real break | neatlogs before | After Trueup's patches | Really |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection cut mid-reply | AI step SUCCESS | AI step ERROR, with the error | Crashed |
| Agent run fails | Agent workflow SUCCESS | Agent workflow ERROR | Crashed |

DISAGREE light: **2 → 0**, and it stayed off on 40 normal real calls. "After" means proposed patches, not merged fixes. neatlogs runs Arize's code for OpenAI Agents, so that fix is [our pull request to Arize](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024), with their maintainer's changes. Our first try stayed 2 → 2: [why, and the traces](docs/witness-before-after.md).

## neatlogs' own email got it wrong

neatlogs' daily email said 6.2% of our runs failed. We checked all 81: 9 had crashed, **11.1%**. These were test runs we crashed on purpose, recorded by released neatlogs, Arize and Traceloop code. The tracing code missed the crashes; the email only added up what it was given. [Every run](docs/neatlogs-email.md).

[Evidence page](docs/index.html) · [Build record](hackathon.md) · [cfo.ai plan](https://cfo.ai/s/a9JKll8UYmSHs7-F)

Trueup's offline lab: 32 confirmed findings, five proven patches across neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry.

import contextlib
import contextvars
import json
import os
import re
import threading
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Iterator

from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import ReadableSpan, SpanProcessor, TracerProvider

_current: contextvars.ContextVar["Run | None"] = contextvars.ContextVar("trueup_witness_run", default=None)
_installed = False
_lock = threading.Lock()


@dataclass
class Call:
    route: str
    status: int | None = None
    exception: str | None = None
    stream: bool = False
    stream_done: bool | None = None
    error_event: bool = False
    body: bytearray = field(default_factory=bytearray)
    overhead_us: float = 0.0


@dataclass
class Run:
    name: str
    calls: list[Call] = field(default_factory=list)
    spans: list[ReadableSpan] = field(default_factory=list)
    app_exception: str | None = None
    disagreements: list[dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)


class _Processor(SpanProcessor):
    def on_start(self, span: Any, parent_context: Any = None) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        return

    def on_end(self, span: ReadableSpan) -> None:
        active = _current.get()
        if active is not None:
            active.spans.append(span)

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        return

    def force_flush(self, timeout_millis: int = 30000) -> bool:  # noqa: ARG002
        return True


class _SyncStream:
    def __init__(self, inner: Any, call: Call) -> None:
        self.inner, self.call = inner, call

    def __iter__(self):
        try:
            for chunk in self.inner:
                _observe(chunk, self.call)
                yield chunk
        except Exception as error:
            self.call.exception = type(error).__name__
            self.call.stream_done = False
            raise

    def close(self) -> Any:
        return self.inner.close()


class _AsyncStream:
    def __init__(self, inner: Any, call: Call) -> None:
        self.inner, self.call = inner, call

    async def __aiter__(self):
        try:
            async for chunk in self.inner:
                _observe(chunk, self.call)
                yield chunk
        except Exception as error:
            self.call.exception = type(error).__name__
            self.call.stream_done = False
            raise

    async def aclose(self) -> Any:
        return await self.inner.aclose()


def _observe(chunk: bytes, call: Call) -> None:
    call.body.extend(chunk)
    compact = chunk.replace(b" ", b"")
    if b"data: [DONE]" in chunk or b'"type":"message_stop"' in compact or b'"type":"response.completed"' in compact:
        call.stream_done = True
    if b'"type":"error"' in compact or b'event: error' in chunk:
        call.error_event = True


def _provider_path(url: Any) -> bool:
    path = str(getattr(url, "path", url)).lower()
    return any(x in path for x in ("/chat/completions", "/responses", "/messages"))


def _patch_http(module: Any) -> None:
    if getattr(module.Client.send, "__trueup_witness__", False):
        return
    sync_original, async_original = module.Client.send, module.AsyncClient.send

    class SyncStream(module.SyncByteStream):
        def __init__(self, inner: Any, call: Call) -> None:
            self.inner, self.call = inner, call
        def __iter__(self):
            try:
                for chunk in self.inner:
                    _observe(chunk, self.call); yield chunk
            except Exception as error:
                self.call.exception = type(error).__name__; self.call.stream_done = False; raise
        def close(self) -> Any:
            return self.inner.close()

    class AsyncStream(module.AsyncByteStream):
        def __init__(self, inner: Any, call: Call) -> None:
            self.inner, self.call = inner, call
        async def __aiter__(self):
            try:
                async for chunk in self.inner:
                    _observe(chunk, self.call); yield chunk
            except Exception as error:
                self.call.exception = type(error).__name__; self.call.stream_done = False; raise
        async def aclose(self) -> Any:
            return await self.inner.aclose()

    def send(client: Any, request: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        active = _current.get()
        if active is None or not _provider_path(request.url):
            return sync_original(client, request, *args, **kwargs)
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        call = Call(route=str(request.url.path), stream=bool(kwargs.get("stream")))
        active.calls.append(call)
        try:
            response = sync_original(client, request, *args, **kwargs)
            call.status = response.status_code
            response.stream = SyncStream(response.stream, call)
            return response
        except Exception as error:
            call.exception = type(error).__name__
            raise
        finally:
            call.overhead_us += (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1000

    async def asend(client: Any, request: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
        active = _current.get()
        if active is None or not _provider_path(request.url):
            return await async_original(client, request, *args, **kwargs)
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        call = Call(route=str(request.url.path), stream=bool(kwargs.get("stream")))
        active.calls.append(call)
        try:
            response = await async_original(client, request, *args, **kwargs)
            call.status = response.status_code
            response.stream = AsyncStream(response.stream, call)
            return response
        except Exception as error:
            call.exception = type(error).__name__
            raise
        finally:
            call.overhead_us += (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1000

    send.__trueup_witness__ = asend.__trueup_witness__ = True
    module.Client.send, module.AsyncClient.send = send, asend


def _attach(provider: Any) -> None:
    if isinstance(provider, TracerProvider) and not getattr(provider, "_trueup_witness", False):
        provider.add_span_processor(_Processor())
        provider._trueup_witness = True


def watch() -> bool:
    """Install Witness once. It fails open and can be disabled with TRUEUP_WITNESS=0."""
    global _installed
    if os.environ.get("TRUEUP_WITNESS", "1").lower() in ("0", "false", "no"):
        return False
    with _lock:
        if _installed:
            return True
        import httpx
        _patch_http(httpx)
        try:
            import httpx2
            _patch_http(httpx2)
        except ImportError:
            pass
        try:
            import neatlogs
            from neatlogs._wrap_utils import get_neatlogs_provider
            _attach(get_neatlogs_provider())
            original = neatlogs.init
            if not getattr(original, "__trueup_witness__", False):
                def init(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any):
                    result = original(*args, **kwargs)
                    _attach(get_neatlogs_provider())
                    return result
                init.__trueup_witness__ = True
                neatlogs.init = init
        except Exception:
            pass
        _installed = True
    return True


def _attrs(span: ReadableSpan) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return dict(span.attributes or {})


def _llm_spans(spans: list[ReadableSpan]) -> list[ReadableSpan]:
    return [s for s in spans if _attrs(s).get("neatlogs.span.kind") == "llm"]


def _has_exception(span: ReadableSpan) -> bool:
    return any(getattr(e, "name", "") == "exception" for e in span.events)


def _truth(call: Call) -> dict[str, Any]:
    raw = bytes(call.body)
    events = []
    for match in re.finditer(rb"(?:^|\n)data:\s*([^\n]+)", raw):
        if match.group(1).strip() != b"[DONE]":
            try: events.append(json.loads(match.group(1)))
            except ValueError: pass
    if not events and raw:
        try: events = [json.loads(raw)]
        except ValueError: pass
    refusal, tools, usage = [], [], None
    for event in events:
        obj = event.get("response", event)
        usage = obj.get("usage") or event.get("usage") or usage
        for choice in event.get("choices", []):
            msg = choice.get("message") or choice.get("delta") or {}
            if msg.get("refusal"): refusal.append(msg["refusal"])
            tools += [x.get("function", {}).get("name") for x in msg.get("tool_calls", [])]
        for item in obj.get("output", []) or []:
            if item.get("type") in ("function_call", "tool_call"): tools.append(item.get("name"))
        for block in obj.get("content", []) or []:
            if block.get("type") == "tool_use": tools.append(block.get("name"))
    return {"error": bool(call.exception or (call.status or 0) >= 400 or call.error_event or call.stream_done is False),

# Witness live result

These are real provider calls: Claude Haiku and the OpenAI Agents SDK through the event's LiteLLM endpoint. No
practice server was used. "After" means Trueup's proposed patches, not merged upstream fixes.

| Kind of break | neatlogs before | neatlogs after Trueup's proposed patches | Really |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection cut mid-reply (Anthropic stream) | AI step SUCCESS; whole trace listed as success | AI step ERROR, with the exception | Stream cut; app raised `RemoteProtocolError` |
| Agent run fails (server refuses the model) | Agent workflow SUCCESS | Agent workflow ERROR | Run failed; app raised `PermissionDeniedError` |

**DISAGREE light: 2 before → 0 after.** Both "before" traces carry the red `TRACE DISAGREE` step; neither
"after" trace does.

- Cut, before: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/5322259c536eae9651b3f0819bfade85
- Cut, after: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/7304699be40a6194bafc2a45478bcd4f
- Agent, before: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/a4074bff1ff4af7caa62e015cae9c3f5
- Agent, after: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/83f710d188f00e206a8b2339e0560443

**No false alarms.** 20 normal real calls before the patches and 20 after (7 plain, 6 streamed, 6 with a tool, 1
async each): 0 disagreements. All of this traffic cost $0.0124.

## What "after" is

- The three proven neatlogs patches, applied together to neatlogs 1.4.26 (they fix the cut stream).
- OpenInference's OpenAI Agents processor from our pull request
  [Arize-ai/openinference#4024](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024) at `4352755`, with the
  maintainer's review suggestions applied. `neatlogs.init(instrumentations=["openai_agents"])` runs
  OpenInference's processor, so this one fix repairs the Agents record for neatlogs users and Arize users alike.

neatlogs also has its own OpenAI Agents recorder (`neatlogs.openai_agents_processor()`), with the same bug. We sent
the fix, with 6 tests (2 fail before, all pass after): issue
[neatlogs/neatlogs#206](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/issues/206), pull request
[#207](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/207).

## What is still not perfect

- In the agent run, the AI step is marked ERROR but carries no error details (no exception event). Witness reports
  this as a note, not a disagreement: the record no longer says the opposite of what happened.
- An inner step that is also named "Agent workflow" still ends SUCCESS under the failed workflow.

## Why our first attempt stayed 2 → 2

An earlier run the same morning applied only the three neatlogs patches and reported 2 → 2. It was right not to
claim a fix. Three things were wrong, all now corrected and covered by tests:

1. **The test relay sent a broken reply.** It skipped the stream's `content_block_start`, so the app crashed on
   bad data instead of on a real cut. The relay now sends a well-formed partial reply, then cuts the connection.
2. **Witness was too strict.** It treated "ERROR without error details" as "OK". It now reports the status exactly
   as recorded and lists missing details as a note.
3. **The wrong library was patched for the agent case.** None of the three neatlogs patches touches the Agents
   path, because neatlogs uses OpenInference's code there. The fix is #4024.

Witness also counted its own `TRACE DISAGREE` step as part of the run, which turned one lie into two marks. That
is fixed too (`tests/test_witness.py`).

The earlier records are kept in `evidence/witness/before.json` (`earlier_run`) and `after.json`
(`earlier_attempt`).

## Run it yourself

```
python examples/shop_agent.py --break anthropic-cut   # or --break agent-fail
python examples/witness_normal.py                     # 20 normal calls
```

Both read `TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY`, `TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL` and `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` from the environment. Everything the
demo prints about the record comes from Witness's own comparison, not from the script.
# neatlogs' own daily email got the error rate wrong

On 12 October neatlogs sent its automatic daily summary for the Trueup project
(11 Oct 09:00 → 12 Oct 09:00 UTC). It said:

> 81 recorded requests. Recorded errors rose to 6.2%.

We read every one of those 81 runs back from neatlogs (through its MCP server) and checked each against what
really happened. The email's own numbers add up: 81 runs, 5 marked as errors. But 9 of the runs really crashed.

| Test run | How many | What really happened | What neatlogs recorded |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The AI server fails on the second call (`ag-llm-fails`) | 5 | Crashed | Counted as an error, but the top step of every one still says SUCCESS |
| The AI sends an error halfway through its reply (`oa-resp-stream-error-event`) | 4 | Crashed | Success, 0 errors, so not counted at all |
| A normal reply (`an-stream-helper`) | 4 | Fine | Success (correct) |

**The email said 6.2% of runs failed. The real number was 11.1% (9 of 81).** Four crashes never showed up.

## What this does and does not show

- **These were test runs we crashed on purpose.** They came from Trueup's practice AI server (the fake
  provider), not from real customers or a real AI provider. Car safety tests work the same way: you crash the
  car on purpose to see what the instruments report.
- **The tracing code caused it, not the email.** Some runs were recorded by neatlogs' own SDK, the others by
  Arize's OpenInference and Traceloop's OpenLLMetry, all sending into neatlogs. The email added up the records
  it was given; the records were wrong.
- **These were the released versions, without our fixes.** The same failures are Trueup's confirmed findings:
  - neatlogs: [Agents run shown OK](../evidence/findings/neatlogs-run_status-openai-agents-top-level-span-status-ok/finding.json),
    [stream error event left unmarked](../evidence/findings/neatlogs-run_status-openai-responses-stream-top-level-span-status-unset/finding.json)
  - OpenInference: [Agents run shown OK](../evidence/findings/openinference-run_status-openai-agents-top-level-span-status-ok/finding.json)
    (fix under review in [Arize-ai/openinference#4024](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024))
  - OpenLLMetry: [Agents run shown OK](../evidence/findings/openllmetry-run_status-openai-agents-top-level-span-status-ok/finding.json),
    [stream error shown OK](../evidence/findings/openllmetry-run_status-openai-responses-stream-top-level-span-status-ok/finding.json)

## The runs, so anyone with access can check

All were sent on 12 Oct 2026 between 01:55 and 02:03 UTC by `trueup demo-export`.

| Library | neatlogs session | Crashed, counted as error (top step SUCCESS) | Crashed, recorded as success | Fine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | `demo-neatlogs-20261012T015515Z` | `138533163e28239ec9181a42f7a7f899` | `7ecadf2e0debe934e325f0e8814815b2` | `6041090c2877aa7d78861796ee052fcb` |
| OpenInference | `demo-openinference-20261012T015747Z` | `35a7fc38358b72dda5734a3567395c31` | `c874896c638944221ea13d90494c3a56` | `fbcb88f7e7564fb32c76273111c5ceb0` |
| OpenLLMetry | (no session) | `3ba07caf2cd4224bd1d81920f4e398fc` | | |
| OpenLLMetry | `demo-openllmetry-20261012T020143Z` | `83a4fc673acfe9816accd168dd7e5bf2` | `029b630bada8d07d95ca231831a98e18` | `de77ae4cb62008d961f134034ea8c2e1` |
| OpenLLMetry | `demo-openllmetry-20261012T020238Z` | `f2a92448caa40bfe294b9c6f35f85aaa` | `19abad72c41b7c8d480d05d1496c3638` | `fde3d2e15d302506f5f45820e5612df6` |

The other 68 runs in the window are Trueup's own working steps (planner, fixer, checks). neatlogs recorded all of
them as success. They are not test crashes, and we did not check them one by one.

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os

import trueup.witness

TOOL = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_order", "description": "Look up an order",
                                          "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"order": {"type": "string"}},
                                                         "required": ["order"]}}}]
ASK = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply in five words: is refund lookup ready?"}]
ASK_TOOL = [{"role": "user", "content": "Look up order 1042 with the tool."}]


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--session")
    parser.add_argument("--json-out")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    trueup.witness.watch()
    import neatlogs
    from openai import AsyncOpenAI, OpenAI
    session = args.session or "witness-normal-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name="trueup-witness-normal",
                  instrumentations=["openai"], pii_enabled=False, user_id="jenny-builds", tags=["witness", "normal"])
    key, base = os.environ["TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY"], os.environ["TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL"]
    client, aclient = OpenAI(api_key=key, base_url=base, max_retries=0), AsyncOpenAI(api_key=key, base_url=base, max_retries=0)
    mix = ["plain_sync"] * 7 + ["stream_sync"] * 6 + ["tool_sync"] * 6 + ["plain_async"]
    counts = {k: 0 for k in ("plain_sync", "stream_sync", "tool_sync", "plain_async")}
    disagreements, notes, errors = [], [], []
    try:
        for i, kind in enumerate(mix):
            with neatlogs.trace(name=f"normal-{i:02d}-{kind}", kind="AGENT", session_id=session):
                try:
                    with trueup.witness.run(f"normal-{i}") as run:
                        if kind == "plain_sync":
                            client.chat.completions.create(model="claude-haiku", messages=ASK, max_tokens=16)
                        elif kind == "stream_sync":
                            for _ in client.chat.completions.create(model="claude-haiku", messages=ASK, max_tokens=16,
                                                                     stream=True):
                                pass
                        elif kind == "tool_sync":
                            client.chat.completions.create(model="claude-haiku", messages=ASK_TOOL, tools=TOOL,
                                                           max_tokens=40)
                        else:
                            asyncio.run(aclient.chat.completions.create(model="claude-haiku", messages=ASK,
                                                                        max_tokens=16))

                   "max_tokens": 40, "stream": True}

            next(response.iter_bytes())  # prove the real upstream started before cutting our cable
        partial = (b'event: message_start\ndata: {"type":"message_start","message":{"id":"msg_cut","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[],"model":"claude-haiku","stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":0}}}\n\n'

        self.connection.close()

"""trueup audit <agent.py>: run a user's main() against the fake under one tracing library.

How it works:
  1. Run main() once with plain replies, to see which provider routes it calls.
  2. For each route it called, run main() once per fake scenario on that route
     (errors, cuts, tools, refusal, ...). Other routes keep plain replies.
  3. Compare truth (the fake's log and main()'s outcome) with the spans.

Limits:
  - main() must take no arguments and reach the provider through the openai or
    anthropic SDK, with clients that read OPENAI_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
    (the default). A client with a hard-coded base_url is not redirected.
  - It runs in the library's venv, which has only the tracing library, openai
    and anthropic. A script that needs other packages will not import.
  - The fake answers every call on a route the same way. Agent loops that wait
    for a particular reply may stop early or loop until their own limit.
  - SDK retries are real requests: with the default max_retries a 500 is sent
    three times, and the call count check compares against all of them.
  - There is no scenario expectation, so the "library changed the request"
    note is not produced, and an app that stops reading a stream early is not
    detected (its output is still expected on the span).
"""

"""A small agent for `trueup audit examples/agent.py --library <lib>`.

One chat call; if the model asks for tools, it answers them and asks again.
The client reads OPENAI_BASE_URL, so audit can point it at the fake.
"""

import json

import openai


def main():
    client = openai.OpenAI(max_retries=0)
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Lagos?"}]
    tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object"}}}]
    for _ in range(2):
        r = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=messages, tools=tools)
        msg = r.choices[0].message
        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return msg.content or msg.refusal

Checks your AI agent's records against what really happened, and fixes the tracing code when they disagree.

[![CI](https://github.com/Jennycruzy/trueup/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Jennycruzy/trueup/actions/workflows/ci.yml) · **[Live demo](https://trueup.38-49-216-59.sslip.io/demo)**

**Why.** The dashboard said OK; the agent had crashed. The tracing code that feeds your dashboard can record a crash as a success, and nothing tells you.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/Jennycruzy/trueup && pip install ./trueup
```

## Quick start

```python
import trueup.witness
trueup.witness.watch()          # once, at start-up, before neatlogs.init()

with trueup.witness.run("order-1042") as run:   # one unit of work
    answer = agent.handle(order_id="1042")

run.disagreements   # [] when the record matches what really happened
```

`TRUEUP_WITNESS=0` turns it off. More in [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

## What you see in neatlogs

When the record is wrong, Witness adds a red `TRACE DISAGREE` step to the same neatlogs record, naming what was recorded and what really happened. It sends no prompt or reply text and never breaks your app.

Real Claude Haiku and OpenAI Agents calls, before and after Trueup's fixes:

| Real break | neatlogs before | After | Really |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection cut mid-reply | AI step SUCCESS | AI step ERROR, with the error | Crashed |

1. Witness reads each AI call on the connection itself: status, stream end, errors.
2. It compares that with the step neatlogs recorded for the same call.
3. If they disagree, it adds `TRACE DISAGREE` to the record.
4. Trueup's lab finds the line of tracing code at fault, writes a fix and proves it.

# Getting started

## Install

Python 3.12 or newer.

```
git clone https://github.com/Jennycruzy/trueup
pip install ./trueup
```

To run the demo agents and the tests as well, install the development extras with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```
cd trueup && uv sync
```

## Quick start

Call `watch()` once at start-up, before `neatlogs.init()`. Then wrap each unit of work in `run()`.

```python
import os

import trueup.witness
trueup.witness.watch()          # once, at start-up, before neatlogs.init()

import neatlogs
neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], instrumentations=["openai"])

with neatlogs.trace(name="shop-agent", kind="AGENT"):
    try:
        with trueup.witness.run("order-1042") as run:   # one unit of work
            answer = agent.handle(order_id="1042")
    except Exception:
        pass                    # your app's own error handling; Witness never swallows an error

print(run.disagreements)        # [] when the record matches what really happened
print(run.notes)                # smaller gaps that do not turn the light on
```

- `run()` gives you the run as soon as it starts. `run.disagreements` and `run.notes` are filled in when the
  `with` block ends, including when your code raised.
- Each disagreement is a small dictionary: `field` (what was compared), `record` (what neatlogs recorded),
  `really` (what really happened) and, when Trueup knows the cause, `finding` (the matching Trueup finding).
- Witness never changes what your app sends or receives, and if Witness itself fails, your app carries on.

## Reading the TRACE DISAGREE step in neatlogs

When the record and reality disagree, Witness adds a red step named `TRACE DISAGREE` to the same neatlogs record,
next to the step that is wrong. Its fields say what was compared:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `call_status` | One AI call: neatlogs says SUCCESS (or ERROR), but the call really failed (or succeeded). |
| `run_status` | The whole run: your code raised, but every top step in the record says SUCCESS. |
| `refusal` | The AI refused, but the refusal is missing from the record. |
| `tools` | The AI asked for tools, but the record names different tools or none. |

A missing AI step (the call happened, the record has no step for it) is also reported, with `record` set to
`missing`.

## The neatlogs detection to create

So that you hear about a disagreement without opening each record:

1. In neatlogs, open **Detections** and create a conditional detection that matches steps named
   `TRACE DISAGREE`. Call it `TRACE DISAGREE light`.
2. Open **Alerts** and add a rule for that detection: at least one occurrence. Pick where it should notify you.

## Turning it off

```
export TRUEUP_WITNESS=0
```

`watch()` then does nothing and returns `False`; `run()` still works but has nothing to compare.

## Running the demo agent

`examples/shop_agent.py` is a small shop agent that can be broken on purpose. It uses real AI calls, so it needs
three settings in the environment: `TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY`, `TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL` (an OpenAI-compatible address)
and `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`.

```
uv run python examples/shop_agent.py                        # a normal call: the light stays off
uv run python examples/shop_agent.py --break anthropic-cut  # the connection is cut mid-reply
uv run python examples/shop_agent.py --break agent-fail     # an OpenAI Agents run fails
uv run python examples/witness_normal.py                    # 20 normal calls; expect 0 disagreements
```

Every line the demo prints about the record comes from Witness's own comparison. `--json-out FILE` saves the
verdict. Run either script with `--help` to see its options.

## Checking your own script against the practice AI server

`trueup audit` runs your script's `main()` against Trueup's practice AI server: a local stand-in for OpenAI and
Anthropic that fails on purpose (errors, cut connections, refusals, tool calls). It then compares what really
happened with what the tracing library recorded. No keys are needed.

```
uv run trueup audit examples/agent.py --library neatlogs
```

`--library` is `neatlogs`, `openinference` or `openllmetry`. Your `main()` must take no arguments and call the
`openai` or `anthropic` SDK with a client that reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (the default). The
first run prepares a separate environment for the library, so it takes a little longer. On `examples/agent.py`
with neatlogs it finds one gap: a refusal that was not recorded.

## Checking Trueup's own numbers

```
uv run trueup verify    # recomputes every number from evidence/ and checks every file's checksum
uv run trueup demo      # replays one finding from start to finish, offline
```

# How it works

Trueup has two parts. **Witness** runs inside your app and turns on a light when the record is wrong. **The lab**
runs on a developer's machine, finds out why the record is wrong, and writes and proves the fix.

## Witness

### What it reads

`watch()` hooks into httpx, the HTTP library that the OpenAI and Anthropic Python SDKs use to talk to their
servers. Inside a `run()`, for every call to a chat, responses or messages address, it notes:

- the HTTP status and any connection error;
- for streamed replies, whether the stream reached its proper end (`[DONE]`, `message_stop` or
  `response.completed`) or was cut off, and whether the server sent an error event part-way;
- refusals and the names of the tools the AI asked for.

Bytes pass straight through to your app unchanged. The added time per call was 2.9 microseconds at the median
(4.8 at most) in the live run.

### What it compares

`watch()` also attaches a listener to neatlogs, so every step neatlogs records during a `run()` is copied to
Witness as well. When the run ends, Witness lines up each real AI call with the matching AI step in the record and
asks:

1. **Did it fail?** The call failed (error status, connection error, error event, or a cut stream) but the step
   says SUCCESS, or the other way round.
2. **Did the whole run fail?** Your code raised, but every top step in the record still says SUCCESS.
3. **Refusal and tools.** The AI refused or asked for tools, and the record says something else.
4. **Is the step there at all?** A call happened with no AI step for it.

### When the light turns on

Any "no" above is a **disagreement**: the record says the opposite of what happened. Witness adds a red
`TRACE DISAGREE` step to the same neatlogs record and adds the disagreement to `run.disagreements`.

### Notes

Some gaps are real but do not make the record say the opposite of what happened. Example: the step is correctly
marked ERROR but carries no error details. Witness lists these in `run.notes` and leaves the light off. Witness's
own `TRACE DISAGREE` steps are never compared, so one wrong record gives one mark, not two.

## The lab

### Practice AI server

A local server that answers like OpenAI (chat and responses) and Anthropic (messages), and fails on purpose:
server errors, connections cut mid-reply, error events in a stream, refusals, tool calls, agents that hit their
step limit. It keeps its own log of exactly what it sent. Trueup ships 51 of these test cases and runs them
against neatlogs, OpenInference (Arize) and OpenLLMetry (Traceloop).

### Comparison

For each case, Trueup compares what really happened (the server's log and whether the app raised) with what the
tracing library recorded. Every difference is a possible problem.

### Checker rules

A possible problem becomes a confirmed **finding** only if it passes seven rules:

1. It happens twice in a row, each time in a fresh process.
2. It happens with the library's recommended setup.
3. It happens on the latest release and on the library's main branch.
4. The practice server really sent what Trueup says it sent.
5. The test itself is sound (no shared state, nothing sent anywhere).
6. Another library, or the published OpenTelemetry conventions (the shared standard for these records), shows
   the right behaviour.
7. A script under 40 lines shows it on its own.

Anything that fails a rule is set aside with the reason, never deleted. The result so far: 32 confirmed findings
across the three libraries.

### Fixer

For a finding, Trueup clones the library, finds the code most likely at fault, and asks a model for a small
change plus one new test. Code, not the model, rejects edits outside the library, in its tests, or that do not
compile.

### Verifier

A fix counts only if:

- the new test fails before the change and passes after;
- the library's own test suite shows no new failure;
- the finding's test cases now match what really happened;
- all test cases together show no new difference.

Up to three tries per run; a failed try goes back to the model with the reason. Five fixes have passed so far.

### Upstream drafts

`trueup upstream` writes the issue and pull-request text for a proven fix into `upstream/`. It never posts.
A person checks the latest release, main, and open pull requests, then posts. Three are open today:
[Arize-ai/openinference#4024](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024),
[traceloop/openllmetry#4610](https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry/pull/4610) and
[neatlogs/neatlogs#207](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/207).

### Checking the numbers

`uv run trueup verify` recomputes every number above from `evidence/` and checks every file's checksum.

# Built with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai

## neatlogs

**Recording.** neatlogs records every run of the agent Witness watches, and every run of Trueup's own agent
(planner, checker, fixer, verifier), each as one record with its steps.

**Witness's step lives in the same record.** When Witness finds a disagreement, its red `TRACE DISAGREE` step is
added next to the step that is wrong, so you see the claim and the correction together. See the before and after
records in [witness-before-after.md](witness-before-after.md).

**Detections.** Trueup installs a neatlogs detection group, `Trace truth (by Trueup)`, that flags AI steps marked
SUCCESS with no output, and AI steps with no output or no token count. In the pull of 12 Oct, 10:03 UTC
(`evidence/neatlogs/detections.json`, 30-day window), "LLM output was not recorded" and "LLM succeeded without
output" had 30 hits each, and "LLM token count was not recorded" 14. Rules that need several steps at once ship
as code in `detections/` (`crashed_run_ok.py`, `duplicate_llm_calls.py`). Details: [detections.md](detections.md).

### neatlogs caught problems in Trueup's own agent

Trueup's agent marks its own trouble as named steps, and neatlogs detections match them. Counts are from the same
pull (30-day window).

| Detection | Hits | What it caught | How it was resolved |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Trueup: model reply was not JSON | 31 (26 on 11 Oct, 5 on 12 Oct) | Replies that opened with prose. In the first version 14 of 40 fixer calls were not JSON, and each was retried with the full ~25k-token prompt. | First, Trueup took the first JSON object in the reply. Then it asked the model for JSON replies: two planner runs used 4 calls and one fixer run used 3, with no JSON retry. |
| Trueup: lead withdrawn (own false alarm) | 2 (11 Oct) | The OpenLLMetry check `20261011T180637Z-openllmetry` set aside two possible problems. | Both failed the "latest release and main" rule: already fixed on main. Kept in `withdrawn.json`, not reported as findings. |
| Trueup: fix attempt failed (retried) | 13 (6 on 11 Oct, 7 on 12 Oct) | Fixer tries that did not apply or failed the verifier. | Each failed try went back to the model with the reason. A run whose three tries all failed reported `fixed: false` and replaced no proven fix. |
| Trueup: command could not run (exit 2) | 0 | A Trueup command that could not start. | Nothing to resolve: no hits in the window. |

**27 false alarms of Trueup's own, removed.** Trueup's comparison once expected a finish reason on agent
framework steps where none applies. Comparing the same saved run again with the corrected comparison went from
58 possible problems to 31; all 27 removed ones were of this kind. They stay listed in `withdrawn.json`.

### The model key from neatlogs

neatlogs gave every team at the event a model key: a LiteLLM endpoint (an address that speaks the OpenAI format
and forwards to Claude and other models). Every real call in the live result used it. All 44 live calls (40
normal, 4 breaks) cost $0.0123794.

### neatlogs' own email

neatlogs' daily email said 6.2% of Trueup's runs failed. We checked all 81: 9 had really crashed, 11.1%. The email
added up correctly; the tracing code had recorded crashes as success. These were test runs we crashed on purpose.
[Every run](neatlogs-email.md).

## Entire

**Every fix links to the session that made it.** Each `fixes/<id>/PROVENANCE.md` names the commit that first added
the fix, its Entire record, and the fixer's tries with their cost. Example: the OpenInference fix came from
checkpoint `01M4M8M1GSQ2BM1RX2JKDJHPD6`,
[commit 79210a4 on Entire](https://entire.io/gh/Jennycruzy/trueup/commit/79210a45418246ceb95e2990d1c003b5fbc7b3d9).
All records: [entire.io/gh/Jennycruzy/trueup](https://entire.io/gh/Jennycruzy/trueup).

**Code graph.** To find the code at fault, `src/trueup/fixer/locate.py` first asks Entire's code graph, with the
finding as a sentence, then its callers and impact. The honest result for the three fixes measured: the graph
ranked the patched function 2nd for OpenInference, 6th for OpenLLMetry, and missed it for neatlogs. The fix runs
themselves used the fallback (ripgrep and Python's own parser on functions named by hand).

**What Entire did not record.** Entire recorded the build of Trueup's core: 10 commits from `dadba2f` to
`88fcc91`. The 20 commits from `56d705d` to `6ea4eee` were made in sessions started outside this folder, so they
have no Entire record. We did not create records afterwards. From 12 Oct, about 14:35 UTC, all work is recorded
again. Details in the [build log](../hackathon.md).

## cfo.ai

The business plan, with runway and break-even questions, is on cfo.ai:
[cfo.ai/s/a9JKll8UYmSHs7-F](https://cfo.ai/s/a9JKll8UYmSHs7-F). The inputs are in [cfo-inputs.md](cfo-inputs.md).

**Measured costs**

- Live real calls: $0.0123794 for 44 calls (40 normal, 4 breaks).
- Planner: $0.09 to $0.10 per run.
- Fixer: $5.73 over 11 runs, about $0.52 per run; the run that produced the proven fix cost $0.40.
- Witness's added time: 2.9005 microseconds per call at the median, 4.809 at most.

**Estimates**

- Live demo: $0.00028 per visitor run; at most $0.084 a day, about $2.53 a month at the 300-run daily cap.

**Proposals (no customer has paid)**

- Free: run Witness locally, with a small monthly allowance.
- Team: priced by recorded runs per month, with history, alerts and CI reports.
- Vendor: for tracing companies. Trueup re-runs its lab on every release and delivers what it finds, with tested
  fixes.

# Witness: before and after

**The DISAGREE light went from 2 to 0, with 0 false alarms on 40 normal calls.**

These are real AI calls: Claude Haiku and the OpenAI Agents SDK, through the event's LiteLLM endpoint (an address
that speaks the OpenAI format and forwards to Claude). No practice server was used. "After" means Trueup's proposed
fixes, not merged upstream fixes.

| Kind of break | neatlogs before | neatlogs after Trueup's proposed fixes | Really |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection cut mid-reply (Anthropic stream) | AI step SUCCESS; whole record listed as success | AI step ERROR, with the error | Stream cut; app raised `RemoteProtocolError` |
| Agent run fails (server refuses the model) | Agent workflow SUCCESS | Agent workflow ERROR | Run failed; app raised `PermissionDeniedError` |

Both "before" records carry the red `TRACE DISAGREE` step; neither "after" record does.

- Cut, before: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/5322259c536eae9651b3f0819bfade85
- Cut, after: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/7304699be40a6194bafc2a45478bcd4f
- Agent, before: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/a4074bff1ff4af7caa62e015cae9c3f5
- Agent, after: https://app.neatlogs.com/traces/83f710d188f00e206a8b2339e0560443

**No false alarms.** 20 normal real calls before the fixes and 20 after (7 plain, 6 streamed, 6 with a tool, 1
async each): 0 disagreements. All of this traffic cost $0.0124.

## What "after" is

- The three proven neatlogs fixes, applied together to neatlogs 1.4.26 (they fix the cut stream).
- OpenInference's OpenAI Agents recorder from our pull request
  [Arize-ai/openinference#4024](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/pull/4024) at `4352755`, with the
  maintainer's review suggestions applied. `neatlogs.init(instrumentations=["openai_agents"])` runs
  OpenInference's code, so this one fix repairs the Agents record for neatlogs users and Arize users alike.

neatlogs also has its own OpenAI Agents recorder (`neatlogs.openai_agents_processor()`), with the same bug. We sent
the fix, with 6 tests (2 fail before, all pass after): issue
[neatlogs/neatlogs#206](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/issues/206), pull request
[#207](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs/pull/207).

## What is still not perfect

- In the agent run, the AI step is marked ERROR but carries no error details. Witness reports this as a note, not
  a disagreement: the record no longer says the opposite of what happened.
- An inner step that is also named "Agent workflow" still ends SUCCESS under the failed workflow.

## Why our first attempt stayed 2 → 2

An earlier run the same morning applied only the three neatlogs fixes and reported 2 → 2. It was right not to
claim a fix. Three things were wrong, all now corrected and covered by tests:

1. **The test relay sent a broken reply.** It skipped the stream's `content_block_start`, so the app crashed on
   bad data instead of on a real cut. The relay now sends a well-formed partial reply, then cuts the connection.
2. **Witness was too strict.** It treated "ERROR without error details" as "OK". It now reports the status exactly
   as recorded and lists missing details as a note.
3. **The wrong library was fixed for the agent case.** None of the three neatlogs fixes touches the Agents path,
   because neatlogs uses OpenInference's code there. The fix is #4024.

Witness also counted its own `TRACE DISAGREE` step as part of the run, which turned one wrong record into two
marks. That is fixed too (`tests/test_witness.py`).

The earlier records are kept in `evidence/witness/before.json` (`earlier_run`) and `after.json`
(`earlier_attempt`).

## Run it yourself

```
python examples/shop_agent.py --break anthropic-cut   # or --break agent-fail
python examples/witness_normal.py                     # 20 normal calls
```

Both read `TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY`, `TRUEUP_MODEL_BASE_URL` and `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` from the environment. Everything the
demo prints about the record comes from Witness's own comparison, not from the script. More in
[Getting started](getting-started.md#running-the-demo-agent).

# neatlogs' own daily email got the error rate wrong

**The email said 6.2% of runs failed. The real number was 11.1% (9 of 81).** Four crashes never showed up.

On 12 October neatlogs sent its automatic daily summary for the Trueup project
(11 Oct 09:00 → 12 Oct 09:00 UTC). It said:

> 81 recorded requests. Recorded errors rose to 6.2%.

We read every one of those 81 runs back from neatlogs (through its MCP server, the read access neatlogs offers to
tools) and checked each against what really happened. The email's own numbers add up: 81 runs, 5 marked as
errors. But 9 of the runs really crashed.

| Test run | How many | What really happened | What neatlogs recorded |
|---|---:|---|---|
| The AI server fails on the second call (`ag-llm-fails`) | 5 | Crashed | Counted as an error, but the top step of every one still says SUCCESS |
| The AI sends an error halfway through its reply (`oa-resp-stream-error-event`) | 4 | Crashed | Success, 0 errors, so not counted at all |
| A normal reply (`an-stream-helper`) | 4 | Fine | Success (correct) |

## What this does and does not show

- **These were test runs we crashed on purpose.** They came from Trueup's practice AI server, not from real
  customers or a real AI provider. Car safety tests work the same way: you crash the car on purpose to see what
  the instruments report.
- **The tracing code caused it, not the email.** Some runs were recorded by neatlogs' own SDK, the others by
  Arize's OpenInference and Traceloop's OpenLLMetry, all sending into neatlogs. The email added up the records
  it was given; the records were wrong.
- **These were the released versions, without our fixes.** The same failures are Trueup's confirmed findings:
  - neatlogs: [Agents run shown OK](../evidence/findings/neatlogs-run_status-openai-agents-top-level-span-status-ok/finding.json),
